description: Screen every covered company on its latest period: range filters on metrics, a sort and paging, all applied on the server over the whole universe. A metric is a standardized concept id (from metrics_list, for example income_statement_total_revenues) or a ratio id (gross_margin, operating_margin, net_margin, fcf_margin, revenue_growth_yoy, roe, roa, asset_turnover, current_ratio, debt_to_equity, interest_coverage, eps_basic, eps_diluted, bank and insurer ratios) or a valuation id (market_cap, enterprise_value, pe_ttm, ps_ttm, pb, ev_ebitda_ttm, ev_ebit_ttm, fcf_yield, dividend_yield: the latest IEX close times the screened period, so use period_type ltm for trailing multiples) or a multi-year growth id (revenue_cagr_3y, revenue_cagr_5y, revenue_cagr_10y, net_income_cagr_3y, net_income_cagr_5y: compound annual growth from annual figures, the start matched by year, null when that year is missing or the figures are not positive). Filter bounds are raw values: 0.2 is 20 percent, amounts are in the reporting currency. A company with no value for a filtered metric does not match; when sorting, missing values come last. Each item has the company (with sector and industry), the period screened and one value object with proof per metric, so every number can be cited. data.total is the size of the whole match and data.next_cursor pages through it. as_of screens on what was known on a date. Use it to find or rank companies by fundamentals or valuation instead of calling each company in turn.

as_of.description: Knowledge date or timestamp (YYYY-MM-DD or RFC 3339). The answer is what FinancialMD knew at that instant: only facts whose known interval contains as_of. Omit for the current view.

currency.description: Reporting currency (ISO 4217), e.g. JPY. Amounts are never compared across currencies: a sort or filter on a money column without this screens the currency most companies of the screen report in (USD across the whole universe).

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous page (data.next_cursor).

filters.description: Range filters, all of which must hold. Give min, max or both (inclusive, raw values).

include_stale.description: Keep companies whose latest period ended more than 18 months before as_of (left out by default; each item carries stale).

limit.description: Maximum number of periods or items to return (default 25, at most 200).

metrics.description: Columns to return: concept ids or ratio ids (default: revenue, net income, the three margins, revenue growth, return on equity).

period_type.description: Which latest period to screen: annual (default), quarterly or ltm.

query.description: Optional name or ticker search to narrow the universe.

name: screen

outputSchema.description: The FinancialMD envelope (docs/API.md section 2): data plus meta (request_id, as_of knowledge time, matched company, coverage, pipeline_version, licence, terms, proof_base). Every numeric value inside data is an object with value, unit, currency, period, known interval, restated flag, method and a proof pointing at the filing. On failure the result is isError with an error object instead.

data.description: { items: [{ company { fmd_id, cik, name, country, reporting_template, primary_ticker, primary_mic, sector, industry }, period, stale, currency, values: { <metric id>: value object or null; a ratio over a zero or negative denominator has value null and withheld_reason } }], next_cursor, period_type, metrics: [{ id, kind, label, metric_format, formula }], sort, total, universe, currency (the one reporting currency screened, or null), stale_after_days, excluded { stale, other_currency }, notes }.

error.description: Present only on isError results: the API error code and message plus remedy hints.

meta.description: Request metadata: request_id, as_of, company resolution, coverage, pipeline_version, licence, terms, proof_base.

attribution.description: Citations a source requires on anything shown from the answer.

title: Screen all companies
